2015_084_080415mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of August 4, 2015, 5:30 p.m., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The consent agenda carried the June 23, 2015 minutes -- recording adoption of the 2015-2016 appropriations, the operating millage renewal for the November 3, 2015 special election, and administrative contract extensions through June 30, 2017 -- plus the June 2015 Treasurer's Report showing total disbursements in period of $14,531,973.12. Action items covered probationary contracts for 31 new teachers, appointment of Adrian Dean as Supervisor of Special Education, a Schools of Choice Section 105c resolution for 90 non-resident ninth graders, a revised rental fee schedule, and a $17,500.00 vacant-property study.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, August 4, 2015, 5:30 p.m., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000), cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Consent agenda (Item 5)**
A. Minutes of the June 23, 2015 Board meeting (the agenda index labels this item June 2, 2015). B. Treasurer's Report - June 2015.

**Attached minutes, June 23, 2015**
The public hearing on the 2015-2016 proposed budget ran from 7:00 p.m. to 7:41 p.m. Rick West presented tax values, homestead/non-homestead forecasts, the foundation allowance, enrollment growth and general fund revenues and expenditures, noting review at the June 16th workshop. Mr. Hauff asked about the TRIG grant; Ms. Underwood asked about the Durant Fund settlement. Dr. Philippart said the District must maintain a 10-12% fund balance for cash flow; West said MSBO recommends 15%. Resident Nicholas Cherasaro questioned MESSA premiums. Present: Philippart, Edmunds, Hauff, Schmidt, Underwood; absent: Fleming and Miletti; about 65 in the audience. Twenty-three students were recognized as the inaugural Superintendent's Student Advisory Board, and Raad Alawan and Ed Morykwas for School Life Troy. Resolutions 15-063 through 15-072 each passed Yes 5 / No 0. Adjourned 8:46 p.m.

**Budget resolutions adopted June 23, 2015**
| Fund | 15-070 FY2014-15 amended | 15-071 FY2015-16 |
|---|---|---|
| General Fund | $145,113,344 | $137,945,141 |
| Special Revenue Funds | 8,406,495 | 7,795,216 |
| Debt Service Funds | 54,664,295 | 16,588,938 |
| 2014 Capital Projects | 19,434,618 | 98,866,705 |
| Capital Maintenance | 101,800 | - |

Millage rates adopted with the 2015-16 budget: Non-Homestead general operating 17.8795 mills; Commercial Personal Property 10.9918; Homestead 4.9918; All Properties debt retirement 4.7000. Resolution 15-069 set the operating millage proposal for a Special School Election on November 3, 2015; 15-072 awarded roof assessment consulting to WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. for $99,128.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

The June year-to-date General Fund report shows revenue of $142,313,249 actual against an approved budget of $142,113,297, and expenditures of $142,778,866 actual against $145,113,344 approved, with $450,546 encumbered and $1,883,932 available (1.30%). Excess revenue over expenditures was (3,000,047); fund balance moved from 21,380,015 on June 1, 2015 to $18,379,968 on June 30, 2015. Two Pentamation check registers (ACCTPA21, dated 07/29/2015) follow, one for period 12 totaling 4,204,500.33 and one for period 13 totaling $7,568,347.64.

**Personnel, curriculum, business and other**
Item 6.A recommends probationary contracts for 31 teachers for 2015-2016, with biographical sketches for 29. Item 6.B appoints Adrian Dean as Supervisor, Special Education effective August 10, 2015, without tenure in the administrative position; Dean came from Waterford School District, most recently principal of Kingsley Montgomery School, an Oakland ISD center-based program. Item 7.A adopts a Schools of Choice resolution under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, for 90 non-resident 9th grade students at the International Academy East in 2016-2017. Item 8.A adopts a revised Building Rental fee schedule under policy E-1102 ($20 annual application fee; Athens Auditorium, seating 1575, $230.00 per hour; Troy High Auditorium, seating 760, $200.00). Item 8.B authorizes Great Northern Consulting Group to perform a Phase I pre-sale investigation of five District-owned vacant properties, not to exceed $17,500.00 from the Capital Maintenance Fund. Item 10.A certifies Paula Fleming, Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as MASB Delegate Assembly delegates for October 22-25, 2015, and Item 10.B is a first reading of Board Policy J-3306, Epinephrine Auto-Injectors, for a September vote.

JUNE 23, 2015 MINUTES. The public hearing on the 2015-2016 proposed budget ran 7:00 p.m. to 7:41 p.m. Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Rick West presented tax values and homestead/non-homestead forecasts, the foundation allowance, the increase in student enrollment, and general fund revenues and expenditures, noting review at the June 16th workshop. Mr. Hauff asked about the TRIG (Technology Readiness Infrastructure Grant); Ms. Underwood asked about the Durant Fund settlement. Dr. Philippart said the District must maintain a fund balance of 10-12% for cash flow; West said MSBO (Michigan School Business Officials) recommends 15%. Troy resident Nicholas Cherasaro asked about MESSA premiums and Blue Cross/Blue Shield quotes. Present: Philippart, Edmunds, Hauff, Schmidt, Underwood; absent: Fleming and Miletti; also Superintendent Machesky and administrators Dziatczak, Griffor, Haezebrouck and West, with approximately 65 audience members. Twenty-three students from Athens High School, International Academy-East, Niles Community High School and Troy High School were recognized as the inaugural Superintendent's Student Advisory Board; Raad Alawan and Ed Morykwas were recognized for School Life Troy. Machesky noted a Cabinet Retreat July 14 & 15 hosted by Children's Hospital and congratulated Christin Silagy, Director of ELD and Federal Grants. Adjourned 8:46 p.m.; submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

RESOLUTIONS (each Yes 5 / No 0). 15-063 approved the May 5, 2015 minutes, May 19, 2015 workshop minutes, the April and May 2015 Treasurer's Report, and Board Policy B-2002, Compensation and Expenses. 15-064 gave Ms. Jennifer Gottlieb a two-year probationary contract as Director of Student Growth, Equity & Assessment effective July 1, 2015. 15-065 extended the Superintendent's contract July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2017. 15-066 extended contracts for Rick West and Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, through June 30, 2017. 15-067 extended 32 administrative contracts through June 30, 2017, including principals Lara Dixon, Remo Roncone, Joe Duda, Timothy Fulcher, Audra Melton, Joyce Brasington, Janice Brzezinski, Brian Canfield, Tammy DiPonio, Sarah Glasser, Matt Jansen, Stephanie Miller, Melanie Morey, David Pass and Jeremy Whan, directors Kerry Birmingham, Rob Carson, Michael Jolly, Stephanie Maynard and Kris Young, and supervisors John Schiesler and Shawna Veit. 15-068 ratified the June 18, 2015 tentative agreement with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016. 15-069 approved the Operating Millage Proposal (Exhibit A) for a Special School Election on November 3, 2015 run by the Clerk of the County of Oakland, citing the Revised School Code, Michigan Election Law Public Act 116 of 1954 and Public Act 336 of 1993; previously authorized operating millages expire December 31, 2015, and the District sought to continue them and restore millage lost to the Headlee rollback, certifying to the Election Coordinator on or before August 11, 2015 under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, signed by Paula Fleming. 15-070 amended fiscal 2014-15 appropriations: General Fund $145,113,344; Special Revenue Funds 8,406,495; Debt Service Funds 54,664,295; 2014 Capital Projects Fund 19,434,618; Capital Maintenance Fund 101,800. 15-071 adopted fiscal 2015-16: General Fund $137,945,141; Special Revenue Funds 7,795,216; Debt Service funds 16,588,938; 2014 Capital Project Funds 98,866,705; Capital Maintenance Funds zero; millage of 17.8795 mills Non-Homestead, 10.9918 mills Commercial Personal Property and 4.9918 mills Homestead for general operating, plus 4.7000 mills on All Properties for Debt Retirement. 15-072 awarded roof assessment and consulting to WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. for $99,128.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

Item 6.B appoints Mr. Adrian Dean as Supervisor, Special Education effective August 10, 2015, without any tenure in the administrative position. Dean spent 7 years at Waterford School District, first as a behavioral consultant and then as principal of Kingsley Montgomery School, an Oakland ISD center-based program serving approximately 100 students, supervising over 70 employees; he holds an Education Specialist degree from Wayne State University (2009, Autism Spectrum Disorders), an M.A. from Wayne State and a B.S. from Eastern Michigan University. The attached AppliTrack packet (application 128154, submitted 7/22/2015, JobID 18082 at the TSD Services Building) lists his address as 1101 East Cook, Grand Blanc, MI 48439, prior annual salaries of $103,000, $75,000, $63,000 and $68,000, certificate IF0000000299357 expiring 06/30/2019, references John Silveri, Nadine Milostan and John Gregory of Waterford and Kathy Barker of Oakland Schools - ISD, and Wayne State transcripts showing a Master of Arts awarded 15-DEC-2005 and an Education Specialist Certificate awarded 22-DEC-2009. Roughly 99 applicants are listed.

CURRICULUM, BUSINESS AND OTHER. Item 7.A adopts a Schools of Choice resolution under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepting 2016-2017 applications from 90 non-resident 9th grade students in districts in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, for the International Academy East. Item 8.A adopts a revised Building Rental fee schedule under policy E-1102, Use of School Buildings and Facilities; fees are hourly with a one-hour minimum plus a $20 annual application fee. Elementary / middle / high: classrooms $20.00 / $20.00 / $30.00; media center $35.00 / $40.00 / $50.00; cafeteria $50.00 / $60.00 / $75.00; gymnasium $55.00 / $65.00 / $80.00. Large Group Instruction (elementary) $40.00; Troy High lecture room seating 80 $50.00; auxiliary gymnasium $70.00; Athens sports decks $55.00; pool and locker rooms $150.00; music, band, green room or choir room $40.00 middle and $45.00 high; Athens Auditorium seating 1575 $230.00; Troy High Auditorium seating 760 $200.00; stage-only rehearsals $150.00 with Theatre Manager approval. Turf, ancillary / community / private: practice $50.00 / $50.00 / $100.00; game without admission $75.00 / $100.00 / $150.00; game with admission $100.00 / $130.00 / $180.00; lights no charge or $22.00. Services, standard / overtime and Saturday / Sunday and holidays: custodial $18.00 / $25.00 / $36.00; grounds $25.00 / $38.00 / $50.00; theatre manager $40.00 / $60.00 / $80.00; theatre technicians and stage manager $15.00 and $20.00. Snow removal, full service / salting only / traction control: elementary $300.00 / $150.00 / $75.00; middle $650.00 / $250.00 / $150.00; high $850.00 / $475.00 / $275.00; IAE / Niles Center $500.00 / $200.00 / $125.00. Item 8.B accepts Phase I of a July 29, 2015 proposal from Great Northern Consulting Group, 1785 W. Stadium, Suite 202, Ann Arbor, Michigan 48103, signed by President William Bowman and addressed to Rick West, covering five vacant District sites (Section 1 Square Lake and John R; 18 acres north of Long Lake between Rochester and John R; 15 and 20 acres north of Wattles east of Livernois; 19.5 acres east of I-75; 18 acres north of Big Beaver west of John R), not to exceed $17,500.00 from the Capital Maintenance Fund; Phase II is estimated at $4,000.00, Phase III shall not exceed $60,000.00, Phase IV will not exceed $12,000, and billing runs $185.00 per hour for principal time and $125.00 for support personnel. Item 10.A certifies Paula Fleming, Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2015 Delegate Assembly during the MASB Fall Conference, October 22-25, 2015, at the Grand Traverse Resort on Thursday, Oct. 22, 2015 at 7:30 p.m. Item 10.B is a first reading of Board Policy J-3306, Epinephrine Auto-Injectors (Epi-Pens), under Student Health J-3300: Michigan's Public Acts 186 and 187 require at least two epi-pens in each school building, and counsel reviewed the draft against MCL 380.1178, MCL 380.1178a and MCL 380.1179, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code. It allows student possession with prescriber and parent approval and a written emergency care plan by a physician licensed in this state; requires at least two trained employees where instructional and administrative staff number at least ten and at least one where fewer than ten, trained under a licensed registered professional nurse; requires at least two unexpired epi-pens per building; authorizes administration to a prescribed student and to any individual on school grounds believed to be having an anaphylactic reaction; requires prompt parent notification; and directs the Superintendent to issue rules consistent with 2013 PA 187 and the Michigan Department of Education's Medication Administration Guidelines. Legal reference MCL 380.1178-1179 (2013 PA 187); a vote is planned on the September consent agenda.
